transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-16
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Priya Rao (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (KeenBridge CTO), Meera Patel (KeenBridge Platform), Omar Haddad (KeenBridge Security), Rina Soto (KeenBridge DevOps)

Summary (auto):
- Focus: marketplace listing auth flow, hybrid/private deployment constraints, and quantization pilot for cost/perf tradeoffs.
- Agreed next steps: share marketplace auth snippet, run quant pilot on staging, follow-up canary test.

Topics: marketplace auth (SAML/SSO & token exchange), VPC + KMS integration, on-prem vs hosted routing, quantization options (8-bit vs 4-bit), batching and KV cache behavior, benchmarks & canary rollout plan.

Action Items (from meeting):
- See metadata action_items for owner/due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya Rao: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We're about 48 minutes, we'll try to walk through the auth flow, the quant pilot plan and any networking constraints. Quick introductions?
[00:12] Daniel Kim: Daniel here, CTO at KeenBridge. We have Meera, Omar and Rina on the line. We're mainly trying to figure out how Redwood's marketplace listing will play with our SSO and KMS requirements.
[00:24] Meera Patel: yep, and also looking at cost — we want to see if quantization helps enough without hurting accuracy for our summarization workload.
[00:32] Marcus Lee: cool, Marcus from Redwood infra. I'll walk through the auth exchange and then show what the quant pilot would look like. Heads up, some of the slide text in the deck auto-transcript may be off — I uploaded the compact deck here: https://redwood.ai/s/keenbridge-marketplace-deck
[00:45] Rina Soto: got it, thanks.
[00:48] [00:48] Marcus Lee: okay first, marketplace auth — there are two common patterns we recommend: 1) listing as a SaaS integration where customers authenticate to Redwood using SAML/SSO and we mint short-lived API tokens on their behalf, or 2) private deployment where the customer runs our runtime in their VPC and uses private mTLS + their KMS.
[01:10] Omar Haddad: quick q — if we go SaaS listing path, how granular is the audit log? We need per-request audit and token binding to user IDs for compliance.
[01:20] Lina Park: good question. For hosted API we emit request-level logs with token meta and route id. We can stage longer retention as an add-on. There's a note about token-level cost traces in the console.
[01:31] Daniel Kim: and for KMS — we have strict key import rules, HSM backed. Can Redwood integrate with external KMS or do you require keys in your control plane?
[01:42] Priya Rao: short answer: for marketplace hosted listings, Redwood holds the ephemeral signing keys; customers can choose Redwood-managed KMS or use customer-managed KMS via an integration. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) the keys remain with you. We should capture Omar's exact KMS requirements in the doc.
[01:59] Meera Patel: ok. Another thing — do your private deploys support our internal helm charts and init containers? We have an init that mounts secrets from Vault.
[02:10] Marcus Lee: yes, our private package is a Helm chart. Customers often add an init container to sync secrets from Vault; we also have a reference for KMS env var mappings. I'll attach the helm snippet in the follow-up.
[02:25] [02:25] Rina Soto: on networking, we need to ensure egress is limited — we can't allow outbound calls to unknown redwood endpoints from prod. How does the listing do routing for hosted fallback?
[02:36] Lina Park: routing policies can be configured per-tenant. For strict egress, you'd want private deployment. For hosted with strict egress, we can set up a VPC peering or an allowlist for specific endpoints. But note there is a tiny latency delta.
[02:51] Daniel Kim: understood. Let's talk quantization — Meera can you explain the workload?
[02:58] Meera Patel: sure. It's a multi-document summarization pipeline, avg input tokens ~1.2k, output 150 tokens. Latency sensitivity is moderate; throughput matters during nightly batch runs. We're testing accuracy drop at 8-bit and 4-bit.
[03:14] Marcus Lee: great. For that profile, continuous KV caching plays a big role — if you plan on repeating context we can save tokens. Note: internal tests: 8-bit (int8) quant usually gives small quality loss, 4-bit (4-bitINT or nf4) is more aggressive. Also we sometimes say 'kv cache' in docs but the auto transcript spells it 'K-V cash' — sorry for any confusion.
[03:36] Omar Haddad: does Redwood's runtime support nf4 quant type and is it validated?
[03:40] Marcus Lee: yes — nf4 and q4_0 are supported on our runtimes with certain kernels. Performance varies by GPU. We'll provide a quantization runbook and perf matrix.
[03:51] [03:51] Marcus Lee: demo plan for pilot: we spin a staging endpoint in your VPC with 4x A10s, configure the model variants (fp16 baseline, int8, q4_0) and run a PRF suite against your prompt set. We measure latency p50/p90, token cost, and accuracy deltas.
[04:10] Meera Patel: timeline? We want results before EOD July 25 if possible.
[04:14] Priya Rao: that fits — Marcus: can you lead the runbook and Lina attach the helm snippet?
[04:19] Marcus Lee: yep I'll publish the runbook by Monday 7/20.
[04:22] Lina Park: I'll add the chart snippet and a tiny example for vault init.
[04:25] [04:25] Daniel Kim: for benchmarks, do you run mixed workloads? Our batch and interactive shapes differ a lot.
[04:31] Marcus Lee: we'll set up two phases: 1) batch night-run with larger seq len and bigger batch size, 2) interactive latency profile for p50/p95. We'll include continuous batching/cold start numbers.
[04:45] Rina Soto: we need to be explicit about fallback behavior — if quant variant fails quality checks in prod, can requests route to hosted full-precision or to a different region?
[04:56] Priya Rao: yes your routing policy can failover to a pinned fp16 model in either a hosted or private variant. For marketplace deployments we recommend a canary policy with 5-10% traffic for new quant variants.
[05:10] Omar Haddad: security question — token binding and session revocation: if a user is deprovisioned in our IdP, how quickly can Redwood revoke tokens? We need near-real-time, within a minute ideally.
[05:22] Lina Park: we support token revocation hooks and a short TTL for minted tokens; for near-real-time you'd use a push endpoint from your IdP to Redwood or use a private deployment where you control token issuance. There's some nuance with cache TTLs. We'll include exact TTL recommendations in the doc.
[05:41] Meera Patel: about metrics — can we get per-model per-tenant token cost breakdowns?
[05:46] Priya Rao: yes console exposes token-level cost numbers and model-level breakdowns, but for marketplace listing usage is aggregated unless you enable tenant-level telemetry retention add-on.
[05:58] [05:58] Marcus Lee: quick note on quant accuracy testing: recommend synthetic perturbation tests and a labeled holdout of ~500 prompts to detect regressions. We'll share our eval harness.
[06:13] Daniel Kim: cool. Anything about licensing in the marketplace listing? We have to pass legal's checklist about data residency and model IP usage.
[06:21] Priya Rao: noted — marketplace listing will include a customer terms block; for regulated customers we usually go to a private deployment SLA. Legal docs: we'll share standard marketplace SOW and a carve-out for data residency.
[06:33] Rina Soto: on the networking side, we'd like a test that simulates our NAT egress and limited ports. Can Redwood run the canary from a customer-like network?
[06:42] Marcus Lee: yes we can run a network emulation test during the pilot. We'll coordinate ports and IP ranges.
[06:48] [06:48] Meera Patel: small nit — some of your sample config references seq_len 2048; our docs use 4096 in some jobs. Will that change kernel selection?
[06:56] Marcus Lee: kernel selection picks different kernels for >2048 sequences on some GPUs. We'll include recommended seq_len buckets. Also note memory/perf tradeoffs with large KV caches.
[07:10] Omar Haddad: about KMS again, do you support key wrapping where Redwood never sees plaintext keys?
[07:16] Lina Park: yes for private deploy we have customer-managed KMS integration and key-wrapping support; for hosted, we can do a bring-your-key flow but it depends on the marketplace constraints — will confirm in writing.
[07:29] Daniel Kim: sounds good. Is there any known issue w/ A10s and nf4 kernels? We saw some throughput cliffs in internal tests with other vendors.
[07:39] Marcus Lee: A10 shows good perf for nf4 in our internal runs but there are config-dependent cliffs, usually around certain batch sizes and sequence combos. We'll surface previous perf traces.
[07:50] [07:50] Priya Rao: ok, let's talk deliverables. Marcus, runbook & perf matrix by 7/20. Lina, helm snippet + vault example by 7/18. Meera, provision staging with 4x A10 by 7/22. Omar, compliance/KMS checklist by 7/19.
[08:08] Meera Patel: yes. We'll try to carve out 8 hours for the pilot runs the week of 7/21.
[08:15] Rina Soto: one more ops ask — if we do private listing, how are updates delivered and who performs them? We want clear patch windows.
[08:24] Lina Park: for private deploys, customers can opt into Redwood-managed updates (we operate the control plane in your VPC) or self-managed updates where you pull new Helm charts. We'll document both workflows and suggest an automated canary.
[08:38] Daniel Kim: can we see RBAC examples? Our SREs want granular roles for who can roll models.
[08:44] Marcus Lee: yes, our console supports token scopes and RBAC; I'll include sample YAML roles.
[08:49] [08:49] (brief cross-talk)
[08:52] Omar Haddad: compliance: for SOC2, does Redwood publish a shared responsibility matrix for marketplace customers?
[08:58] Priya Rao: yes we have an SRM that we share during legal/ procurement; will attach to the follow-up.
[09:06] Meera Patel: any concerns about cold start when switching to a larger seq_len?
[09:11] Marcus Lee: cold starts are mostly kernel initialization and KV cache warm-up; for canary we recommend a warm-up phase with synthetic traffic.
[09:20] Daniel Kim: ok -- minor point: can you also include a short snippet showing how to pin a model version in the listing so we can rollback quickly?
[09:27] Priya Rao: absolutely. We'll include pinning + automatic fallback policy examples.
[09:33] Marcus Lee: last technical nuance — some of the quant libraries we use have slightly different logits scaling; for fidelity checks use both BLEU-ish metrics and human reviews.
[09:44] Meera Patel: noted, we'll prep a 500-sample holdout.
[09:48] [09:48] Priya Rao: great. Any blockers we haven't listed?
[09:52] Daniel Kim: nothing immediate; legal will want a quick review of the marketplace doc but that's expected.
[09:57] Rina Soto: can you also confirm retention windows for request logs in hosted mode? We need 13 months in some cases.
[10:04] Lina Park: retention add-on covers longer windows; default is 90 days, add-on supports 13 months with log export hooks to your S3.
[10:15] Meera Patel: ok thanks.
[10:17] Priya Rao: quick recap: we will send marketplace auth doc, helm snippet, quant runbook, perf matrix, SRM and legal starter docs. Follow-up: pilot kickoff week of 7/21.
[10:30] Daniel Kim: perfect. Thanks everyone.
[10:33] (meeting ends)
